mapping_status: Researcher-constructed CAPEC-informed 12-group partition; neither expert certified nor an official CICIoT-to-CAPEC crosswalk.

original_vs_new_taxonomy.scope: Keep the original eight-family primary method separate from this twelve-group standards control. The older broad ATT&CK tactic control is also not this CAPEC mechanism partition.

coverage.claim_boundary: Reference coverage is not exact mechanistic validity, expert agreement, per-flow evidence, or official dataset-to-CAPEC annotation. Conditional secondary candidates remain explicitly conditional.

mechanism_groups.definition: Host, port, OS or vulnerability discovery; no unsupported probe subtype or attack stage.
Nonattack singleton; no CAPEC attack annotation.
Dictionary-based password guessing; not password spraying or credential stuffing.
Protocol fragmentation; ACK flooding is only a partial CAPEC match.
HTTP request flooding or low-rate session holding, with distinct CAPEC references.
ICMP flooding without a specific message subtype claim.
Command, SQL and browser-script injection; conditional subtypes remain conditional.
Broad flooding fallback for generator labels lacking a supported exact CAPEC child.
TCP flooding at protocol level; resource subtype not inferred from DoS versus DDoS.
DNS spoofing or ARP adversary-in-the-middle; no inferred credential-theft outcome.
UDP flooding; neither reflection nor amplification inferred.
Explicit unresolved fallback, not an official mechanism or validated web-shell/backdoor technique.

per_label_mapping.basis: A malware/backdoor label is compatible with malicious logic in a deployed component.
per_label_mapping.limitation: Insertion path, execution, persistence and remote-access technique are unresolved. This is an explicit fallback bucket, not an official mechanism category.

per_label_mapping.basis: Untrusted input changes interpreted commands; CAPEC-248 is general command injection.

source_citation.apa_reference: The MITRE Corporation. (2023, January 24). Common Attack Pattern Enumeration and Classification (CAPEC) (Version 3.9) [Attack-pattern catalog]. https://capec.mitre.org/data/xml/capec_v3.9.xml
source_citation.scope: Citation evidence added after design lock. Does not amend frozen mapping, roles, configuration, source_manifest, or experiment results.

run_metadata.uncertainty: Six overlapping grouped random splits: report descriptive mean/SD; not six independent datasets or time-held-out cohorts.
run_metadata.cost_scope: new hierarchy only; flat training/inference cost excluded because predictions reused; no physical-edge or energy experiment

interpretation_limits: Six overlapping grouped random splits; mean and sample SD are descriptive, not independent-sample confidence intervals.
Control selected and frozen using capped-fit counts, never test-based map selection.
CAPEC reference coverage is not mechanistic validity, expert agreement, or per-flow proof.
New hierarchy CPU cost excludes reused flat training/inference and is not physical-edge latency, feature-extraction throughput, or energy.
Runner serialization_seconds also includes scoring and must not be interpreted as isolated serialization cost.
NF-ToN-IoT-v3 disjoint chronological attack support is a separate extrapolation boundary, not rare-class replication evidence; no NF experiment is performed in this subtask.
No physical edge device was available and no physical-edge experiment was performed.
